missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Доллар' is a masculine noun in the nominative as the subject of 'подорожал'. 'Сегодня' marks the time, and 'немного' softens the verb. A natural finance-news phrase.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Доллар' is the inanimate masculine accusative direct object of 'нашёл', identical to the nominative. 'На улице' is prepositional. A simple narrative sentence.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Доллара' is the masculine genitive after 'нет', reinforced by 'ни'. The phrase emphasizes having no money at all. A common emphatic negation.

missions.phrase: Цена выросла к доллару на рубль.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Dative with preposition. 'Доллару' is the dative form after 'к', marking the reference point of comparison. 'На рубль' shows the amount. A natural currency-comparison phrase.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Долларом' is the instrumental marking the means of payment. 'Одним' agrees in the masculine instrumental. A clean instrumental example for transactions.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Долларе' is the prepositional form after 'о', the topic of conversation. 'Все' is the subject, and 'сегодня' adds the time. A reliable prepositional model.

missions.phrase: У меня в кармане два доллара.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Genitive singular after a number. After 'два' the noun takes the genitive singular 'доллара'. 'В кармане' is prepositional. A core counting pattern with money.

Strategic focus: Accusative plural. 'Доллары' is the inanimate accusative plural after 'на', matching the nominative plural. 'Рубли' is the accusative object exchanged. A practical exchange-office phrase.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Долларов' is the genitive plural after 'много', taking the hard-stem ending. 'Старых' agrees, and 'в кошельке' is prepositional. A core quantity pattern.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Доллары' is the nominative plural subject of 'лежат'. 'Эти' agrees in the plural, and 'в банке' is prepositional. A clean plural statement.
